text: Below is a comprehensive listing of all Mechanical Engineering courses offered for undergraduate (B.Eng.) and graduate (M.Eng.) students. Each entry includes the course code, title, description, prerequisites, and assigned credit hours.
path: Cendara University > Department of Mechanical Engineering > Course Catalog > B.Eng./M.Eng. in Mechanical Engineering

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
An overview of the field of mechanical engineering, including its history, fundamental principles, and modern applications. Topics include major subdisciplines, an introduction to engineering ethics, and industry practices.
Prerequisites: None
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 101: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering

text:
Credits: 4
Description:
Fundamental skills in technical drawing, computer-aided design (CAD), and blueprint reading. Introduction to CAD software for creating, annotating, and analyzing engineering designs.
Prerequisites: None
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 111: Engineering Graphics & CAD

text:
Credits: 4
Description:
Covers the fundamentals of statics, including force systems, equilibrium, structural analysis, centroids, and moments of inertia. Designed for engineering problem-solving.
Prerequisites: MATH 120 (Calculus I)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 122: Engineering Mechanics I – Statics

text:
Credits: 4
Description:
Study of particles and rigid bodies in motion, Newton’s laws, kinematics, kinetics, work and energy, impulse and momentum.
Prerequisites: MECH 122 (Engineering Mechanics I)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 123: Engineering Mechanics II – Dynamics

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
Explores the structures, properties, testing, and applications of metals, polymers, ceramics, and composites. Discussion of selection criteria for materials in mechanical systems.
Prerequisites: CHEM 105 (General Chemistry I)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 201: Materials Science for Engineers

text:
Credits: 4
Description:
Introduces the first and second laws of thermodynamics, basic thermodynamic properties, simple systems, energy transformations, and entropy concepts.
Prerequisites: PHYS 130 (General Physics I); MATH 121 (Calculus II)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 231: Thermodynamics I

text:
Credits: 4
Description:
Study of fluids at rest and in motion, including properties, hydrostatics, conservation laws, and applications to engineering systems.
Prerequisites: MECH 122 (Engineering Mechanics I), MECH 231 (Thermodynamics I)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 241: Fluid Mechanics

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
Overview of modern and traditional manufacturing processes such as casting, forming, machining, welding, and additive manufacturing. Laboratory demonstrations included.
Prerequisites: MECH 201 (Materials Science)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 252: Manufacturing Processes

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
Application of CAM technologies, programming CNC machines, and process planning in manufacturing. Includes practical exercises using industry-standard CAM software.
Prerequisites: MECH 111 (Engineering Graphics & CAD)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 263: Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM)

text:
Credits: 4
Description:
Integration of mechanical, electrical, and computer systems in intelligent machines. Focus on microcontrollers, sensors, actuators, and system integration.
Prerequisites: EECS 210 (Intro to Electronics), MECH 122 (Engineering Mechanics I)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 272: Mechatronics

text:
Credits: 4
Description:
Covers stress and strain analysis, axial loading, bending, shear, torsion, deflection, and stability of structural members. Laboratory component included.
Prerequisites: MECH 123 (Engineering Mechanics II), MECH 201 (Materials Science)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 321: Mechanics of Materials

text:
Credits: 4
Description:
Advanced concepts in thermodynamics, including cycles for power and refrigeration, mixtures, chemical reactions, and an introduction to heat transfer.
Prerequisites: MECH 231 (Thermodynamics I)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 331: Thermodynamics II

text:
Credits: 4
Description:
Principles of heat conduction, convection, and radiation with engineering applications. Includes numerical analysis of heat transfer problems.
Prerequisites: MECH 231 (Thermodynamics I), MATH 222 (Differential Equations)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 342: Heat Transfer

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
Fundamental approaches in mechanical design, including analysis and selection of mechanical elements such as gears, shafts, and fasteners. Team-based design project.
Prerequisites: MECH 321 (Mechanics of Materials)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 353: Mechanical Design I

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
Advanced topics in product design, reliability, optimization techniques, and design for manufacturability. Capstone design project.
Prerequisites: MECH 353 (Mechanical Design I)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 354: Mechanical Design II

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
Kinematics and dynamics of machines including linkages, cams, gears, and balancing of rotating and reciprocating masses.
Prerequisites: MECH 123 (Engineering Mechanics II)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 371: Dynamics of Machinery

text:
Credits: 2
Description:
Proposal and conceptual design phase of a major team-based engineering project. Emphasis on project planning, literature review, and ethics.
Prerequisites: Senior standing in Mechanical Engineering
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 401: Senior Project I

text:
Credits: 4
Description:
Completion and presentation of a team engineering project, including design, analysis, prototyping, and reporting.
Prerequisites: MECH 401 (Senior Project I)
path: Cendara University > Undergraduate Courses (B.Eng.) > MECH 402: Senior Project II

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
In-depth exploration of thermodynamic theory for complex systems, including exergy analysis, multi-phase systems, and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
Prerequisites: MECH 331 (Thermodynamics II) or equivalent
path: Cendara University > Graduate Courses (M.Eng.) > MECH 510: Advanced Thermodynamics

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
Theory and application of the finite element method for solving mechanical engineering problems in solid mechanics, heat transfer, and fluid flow.
Prerequisites: MECH 321 (Mechanics of Materials); recommended: MATH 350 (Numerical Methods)
path: Cendara University > Graduate Courses (M.Eng.) > MECH 521: Finite Element Analysis

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
Principles of robotics, manipulators, sensor integration, motion planning, and computer vision for automated mechanical systems. Industrial case studies included.
Prerequisites: MECH 272 (Mechatronics) or consent of instructor
path: Cendara University > Graduate Courses (M.Eng.) > MECH 531: Robotics and Automation

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
Covers advanced fluid dynamics topics including compressible flow, boundary layers, turbulence modeling, and computational techniques.
Prerequisites: MECH 241 (Fluid Mechanics)
path: Cendara University > Graduate Courses (M.Eng.) > MECH 542: Advanced Fluid Mechanics

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
Analysis of renewable energy systems, including solar, wind, geothermal, and bioenergy. Focus on engineering design and sustainability assessment.
Prerequisites: MECH 331 (Thermodynamics II) or consent of instructor
path: Cendara University > Graduate Courses (M.Eng.) > MECH 556: Sustainable Energy Systems

text:
Credits: 3
Description:
Dynamic modeling and control of mechanical systems using classical and modern methods. Includes simulation and analysis using MATLAB/Simulink.
Prerequisites: MECH 371 (Dynamics of Machinery); recommended: EECS 305 (Control Systems)
path: Cendara University > Graduate Courses (M.Eng.) > MECH 570: Mechanical Systems Control

text:
Credits: 1
Description:
Weekly seminars on current research topics in mechanical engineering. Participation in research discussions and presentations by faculty and guest speakers.
Prerequisites: Graduate standing in Mechanical Engineering
path: Cendara University > Graduate Courses (M.Eng.) > MECH 590: Research Seminar in Mechanical Engineering

text:
Credits: 2–4
Description:
Individual study or research under faculty supervision in an area of special interest to the student. Requires approval of supervising faculty and department chair.
Prerequisites: Graduate standing; instructor consent
path: Cendara University > Graduate Courses (M.Eng.) > MECH 598: Independent Study

text:
Credits: 6
Description:
Original research under the guidance of a faculty advisor, culminating in a written thesis and oral defense before a faculty committee.
Prerequisites: Completion of at least 18 graduate credits; approval of thesis proposal
path: Cendara University > Graduate Courses (M.Eng.) > MECH 599: Graduate Thesis
